issues.description: The problem statement refers to the animal feeding-sound method as getFeedingSound() (e.g. the Seal task and the feedAllAnimals()/song description), but the template/solution code declares and uses messageOnFeed(). Concretely: problem_statement.md instructs students to implement/get results from getFeedingSound(), while solution/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java declares the abstract method messageOnFeed() and solution/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java calls animal.messageOnFeed(). This naming mismatch is likely to confuse students about which method to implement and which name the tests expect.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across all materials. Prefer updating the problem statement (and its example song placeholders) to refer to messageOnFeed() everywhere to match the UML, template and solution code, and to avoid requiring students to rename methods. Alternatively, if you prefer getFeedingSound(), rename the abstract method in Animal and all its usages (and update tests and UML) to getFeedingSound(). Update all occurrences in problem_statement.md, the UML text, and any examples so a single identifier is used throughout.
